At the same time, the struggling sorority house nearby is being threatened with shutdown, setting up the perfect reason for Shelley to step in and prove everyone wrong.

Funny, awkward, and surprisingly heartfelt, this moment is where Shelley’s real journey finally begins. 💕

snippet.title: 📐 "Soundproof Walls & Murphy Beds"—  Roommate  #shorts
snippet.description:
An architecture presentation. A roommate from hell. And the most PASSIVE-AGGRESSIVE design pitch in history. 😤📐💀

In this absolutely HILARIOUS scene from My Troublemaker Roommate, our protagonist presents her final architecture project — a room designed specifically for her awful roommate Celeste. The features? Murphy beds to increase "livable space." Soundproof walls to block Celeste's lies. And Polaroid twinkly lights just like their room — because Celeste apparently stole the idea. The result is pure comedy GOLD. 😂

The scene opens with the architecture student addressing her class:

🗣️ "Ahh!"

Someone interrupts: "Wait, you hooked up in her bed?"

She pushes through: "Anyways, by installing Murphy beds, we increase the livable space, and it becomes a lot harder for Celeste to run train on a short king while I'm writing her papers." 💀

She mimics Celeste: "Oh, can you taste the kombucha?"

Another student gasps: "Why is that Celeste doll literally me?"

The presenter continues: "So far, this design only benefits me. So, I asked myself, 'What does Celeste need?' It's hard because she had humble beginnings growing up in this house."

Then she reveals her masterpiece:

🗣️ "This is a soundproof partition wall. So now I don't have to hear any more lies about Celeste's dad being a janitor—"

A friend whispers: "Oh my God, dude."

The presenter grins: "Oh, and one more thing. Twinkly lights with Polaroids."

Her friend realizes: "Like our room. She must've got it from…"
Presenter: "Yeah."

She wraps up: "Thank you for listening. Go, architecture."

Then she adds one last jab: "By the way, maybe TAs shouldn't use a class contact sheet as a dating service."

Her friend: "That was insane, but, like, in a good way, of course."

Presenter: "Thanks."

Friend: "Oh, are you gonna be okay in there?"

Presenter: "Yeah. I'll see you guys later." 😏

This scene is PEAK petty revenge comedy. The presenter uses her architecture final to publicly roast her terrible roommate — and the professor and class have no idea (or maybe they do). The "run train on a short king" line is unforgettable. The soundproof wall for janitor-dad lies is brutal. And the Polaroids reveal that Celeste stole their room's aesthetic? Chef's kiss. 👌
